before.title: Local evolution for a strict barotropic perfect fluid: smooth constrained data admit a development, unique up to a data-fixing isometry
before.statement:
Let a perfect-fluid model have smooth equation of state $p=p(\epsilon)$ on an
open interval $J$ with $\epsilon+p>0$ and $0<p'(\epsilon)<1$
([[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]]). Let
$(\Sigma,h,K_2,\epsilon_0,n_0)$ be smooth initial data: a three-manifold
$\Sigma$ with Riemannian metric $h$, symmetric $2$-tensor $K_2$, a smooth
function $\epsilon_0:\Sigma\to J$ and a smooth future-directed unit timelike
vector field $n_0$ on $\Sigma$ (not required to be normal). Suppose the
constraint equations of [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]] hold on
$\Sigma$ with the stress-energy tensor computed from $(\epsilon_0,n_0)$. Then
the data admit a local development in the sense of
[[thm-gr-local-geometric-development]]: a smooth Lorentzian metric $g$, a
smooth function $\epsilon$ and a smooth future-directed unit timelike field $n$
near $\Sigma$ satisfying
$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa\bigl((\epsilon+p)n_an_b+p\,g_{ab}\bigr),\qquad D\epsilon+(\epsilon+p)\vartheta=0,\qquad (\epsilon+p)a^b+h^{ba}\partial_ap=0$$
with $p=p(\epsilon)$ and $D,\vartheta,a,h$ as in
[[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]], with $\Sigma$ spacelike of induced data
$(h,K_2)$ and matter data $(\epsilon_0,n_0)$; and any two developments of the
same data agree near $\Sigma$ up to a data-fixing time-orientation-preserving
isometry.

references.title: H. Friedrich and A. D. Rendall, The Cauchy Problem for the Einstein Equations, Living Reviews in Relativity 3 (2000), article 1 (arXiv:gr-qc/0002074), Section 4.2 (The Einstein-Euler System): the hyperbolic reduction of the Einstein-Euler system, the positivity conditions on specific enthalpy and speed of sound (4.38), the frame variables and their reduced equations, and the pressure-free (dust) subsidiary system of Sections 4.2.4-4.2.5, equations (4.26)-(4.48) and (4.56)-(4.63)

H. Friedrich and A. D. Rendall, The Cauchy Problem for the Einstein Equations, Living Reviews in Relativity 3 (2000), article 1 (arXiv:gr-qc/0002074), Section 5.1 (Local Existence Theorems for the Einstein Equations): harmonic-map gauge, the reduced initial data constructed from (h,chi), the propagation of the gauge by the homogeneous wave system for the gauge residual Delta^alpha, and the local existence theorem

statement.after:
Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Fix $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, $\kappa>0$ and one smooth EOS $p=p(\epsilon)$ on an open interval $J$ with $\epsilon+p>0$ and $0<p'(\epsilon)<1$ ([[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]]). Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth three-manifold with smooth metric $h$, symmetric tensor $K_2$, density $\epsilon_0:\Sigma\to J$ and tangent field $v_0$ with $h(v_0,v_0)<1$. These specify the future unit initial velocity
$$U_0=W_0(N+v_0),\qquad W_0=(1-h(v_0,v_0))^{-1/2}$$
in $\mathcal V=\mathbb RN\oplus T\Sigma$, with metric $g_0(aN+X,bN+Y)=-ab+h(X,Y)$. Require the constraints of [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]] for
$$T_0=(\epsilon_0+p(\epsilon_0))U_0^{\flat_{g_0}}\otimes U_0^{\flat_{g_0}}+p(\epsilon_0)g_0.$$
Then a smooth time-oriented local development has metric $g$, density $\epsilon$ and future unit fluid velocity $u$ satisfying
$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa\left[(\epsilon+p)u_au_b+pg_{ab}\right],\qquad D\epsilon+(\epsilon+p)\vartheta=0,\qquad (\epsilon+p)a^b+\Pi^{ba}\partial_ap=0.$$
Here $D=\nabla_u$, $\vartheta=\nabla_a u^a$, $a=\nabla_u u$ and $\Pi^{ab}=g^{ab}+u^au^b$. Initial geometric data are $(h,K_2)$ and initial matter data are $(\epsilon_0,U_0)$ under $N\mapsto n$, $X\mapsto i_*X$. Arbitrary smooth subluminal tilt is allowed. The initial surface lies in the interior of its intrinsic domain of dependence; its interior Cauchy neighborhood is globally hyperbolic. Any two developments of this same EOS and complete data agree near the entire initial surface by a data-fixing future isometry matching density and velocity. The neighborhood may have position-dependent time width; shocks, vacuum boundaries and vanishing sound speed are outside this strict interior-fluid statement ([[thm-gr-local-geometric-development]]).

citations.quote:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice for the integral below
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let a perfect-fluid model on a Lorentzian manifold
be given with smooth equation of state $p=p(\epsilon)$ defined on an open
interval $J\subseteq\mathbb R$, with $\epsilon+p(\epsilon)>0$ and
$p'(\epsilon)>0$ for all $\epsilon\in J$
([[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]]). Fix a base point
$\epsilon_*\in J$ and define the **barotropic enthalpy variable**
$$r:J\to\mathbb R,\qquad r(\epsilon):=\int_{\epsilon_*}^{\epsilon}\frac{\sqrt{p'(z)}}{z+p(z)}\,dz .$$
The integrand is continuous on $J$ ([[thm-continuous-implies-integrable]]), so
$r$ is well defined and $C^1$ with $r'(\epsilon)=\sqrt{p'(\epsilon)}/(\epsilon+p(\epsilon))>0$
([[cor-ftc-integral-function-differentiable-almost-everywhere]]); hence $r$
maps $J$ diffeomorphically onto the open interval $r(J)$, and we write
$\epsilon(r)$ for its inverse and $c_s:=\sqrt{p'}$ for the **sound-speed
function**, so that $r'(\epsilon)=c_s(\epsilon)/(\epsilon+p(\epsilon))$ and
$c_s\in(0,1)$ when $0<p'<1$ is assumed.

The definition and the two displayed equivalences are the form in which the
fluid system is fed into [[lem-gr-barotropic-fluid-symmetric-hyperbolic-system]];
no existence theorem is asserted here.

Let a perfect-fluid model with smooth equation of state $p=p(\epsilon)$ satisfy
$\epsilon+p>0$ and $0<p'(\epsilon)<1$ on an open interval $J$, let
$r:J\to r(J)$ and $c_s=\sqrt{p'}$ be the enthalpy variable and sound speed of
[[def-gr-barotropic-enthalpy-variable]], and let $D,\vartheta,a^b,h^{ab}$
denote the comoving derivative, expansion, acceleration and rest-space
projection of [[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]]. Then:

**(a)** the perfect-fluid equations
$D\epsilon+(\epsilon+p)\vartheta=0$, $(\epsilon+p)a^b+h^{ba}\partial_ap=0$ are
equivalent to
$$D r+c_s\,\vartheta=0,\qquad D n^b+c_s\,h^{ba}\partial_a r=0 ,$$
and the stress-energy tensor
$T^{ab}=(\epsilon+p)n^an^b+pg^{ab}$ is divergence-free exactly when these
equations hold;

**(b)** in every orthonormal frame $(n,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ at a point, the principal
symbol of the system (a) in the variables $(r,n^1,n^2,n^3)$ at a covector
$\zeta=\zeta_0n^\flat+\zeta_\perp$ is the symmetric matrix
$$A(\zeta)=\begin{pmatrix}\zeta_0&c_s\zeta_\perp^{\mathsf T}\\ c_s\zeta_\perp&\zeta_0 I_3\end{pmatrix};$$
its eigenvalues are $\zeta_0$ (multiplicity two) and
$\zeta_0\pm c_s|\zeta_\perp|$ (multiplicity one each); consequently $A(\zeta)$
is positive definite for every future-directed timelike covector $\zeta$
(because $\zeta_0>|\zeta_\perp|$ and $c_s<1$);

**(c)** consequently the combined Einstein-fluid system, with the reduced
Einstein equation in the harmonic gauge, is a first-order quasilinear symmetric
hyperbolic system with positive definite time matrix, coupled only through
zeroth-order terms in the first derivatives of the metric.

$r:J\to r(J)$ and $c_s=\sqrt{p'}$ be the enthalpy variable and sound speed of
[[def-gr-barotropic-enthalpy-variable]], and let $D,\vartheta,a^b,h^{ab}$
denote the comoving derivative, expansion, acceleration and rest-space
projection of [[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]]. Then:

$D\epsilon+(\epsilon+p)\vartheta=0$, $(\epsilon+p)a^b+h^{ba}\partial_ap=0$ are
equivalent to

and the stress-energy tensor
$T^{ab}=(\epsilon+p)n^an^b+pg^{ab}$ is divergence-free exactly when these
equations hold;

**(b)** in every orthonormal frame $(n,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ at a point, the principal
symbol of the system (a) in the variables $(r,n^1,n^2,n^3)$ at a covector

its eigenvalues are $\zeta_0$ (multiplicity two) and
$\zeta_0\pm c_s|\zeta_\perp|$ (multiplicity one each); consequently $A(\zeta)$
is positive definite for every future-directed timelike covector $\zeta$
(because $\zeta_0>|\zeta_\perp|$ and $c_s<1$);

**(c)** consequently the combined Einstein-fluid system, with the reduced
Einstein equation in the harmonic gauge, is a first-order quasilinear symmetric
hyperbolic system with positive definite time matrix, coupled only through
zeroth-order terms in the first derivatives of the metric.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$ and let $U\subseteq M$ be a nonempty open
matter domain ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]],
[[prop-an-open-subset-of-a-smooth-manifold-has-a-canonical-restricted-smooth-structure]]).

**(a) Dust.** Let $(\rho,u,T)$ be a dust model on $U$
([[def-gr-dust-matter-model]]). Then

$$\nabla^aT_{ab}=0\ \text{on }U\qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad \nabla_a(\rho u^a)=0\ \text{and}\ u^a\nabla_au^b=0\ \text{on }U .$$

**(b) Perfect fluid.** Let $(\varepsilon,p,n,T)$ be a perfect-fluid model on
$U$ with comoving derivative $D$, expansion $\vartheta$, acceleration $a$ and
projection $h$ ([[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]]). Then

$$\nabla^aT_{ab}=0\ \text{on }U\qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad D\varepsilon+(\varepsilon+p)\vartheta=0\quad\text{and}\quad (\varepsilon+p)a^b+h^{ba}\partial_ap=0\ \text{on }U .$$

Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth three-manifold, let $h$ be a smooth Riemannian metric
and $K$ a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor on $\Sigma$
([[def-gr-spacelike-initial-data-and-constraints]]). Let a **matter sector** be
specified as follows: a finite list of tensor fields $\psi$ on a spacetime
carrying $\Sigma$, a smooth stress-energy construction $T(g,\psi)$ and a system
of equations $E(g,\psi)=0$ such that, in every chart, the combined system for
$(\psi,g)$ with the metric variables of
[[lem-gr-reduced-einstein-principal-part]] clause (b) attached is a first-order
quasilinear symmetric hyperbolic system coupled only through zeroth-order terms
in the first derivatives of the metric, and such that $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$ is a
consequence of $E(g,\psi)=0$ on-shell. Suppose smooth initial data $\psi_0$ on
$\Sigma$ are given so that the constraint equations
$$S_h+(\operatorname{tr}_hK)^2-|K|_h^2=2\Lambda+2\kappa\,T(n,n),\qquad \operatorname{div}_hK(Y)-\nabla^h_Y\operatorname{tr}_hK=\kappa\,T(n,Y)$$
hold on $\Sigma$ for the normal vector $n$ and the stress tensor determined by
$(h,K,\psi_0)$ ([[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]]). Then:

**(a)** every $p\in\Sigma$ has an open neighborhood $O_p$ in $\Sigma$ such that
there are an open neighborhood $W_p$ of $O_p$ in a smooth four-manifold, a smooth
Lorentzian metric $g$ and matter fields $\psi$ on $W_p$ solving the field
equations $G+\Lambda g=\kappa T(g,\psi)$ and the matter equations, with
$O_p$ a spacelike embedded hypersurface of induced metric $h$ and second
fundamental form $K$;

**(b)** the local solutions of (a) glue: over a neighborhood $W$ of $\Sigma$
there are $g,\psi$ solving the equations, with $\Sigma$ spacelike of data
$(h,K)$, and $\Sigma$ lies in the interior of its domain of dependence in $W$,
so that $D(\Sigma)\cap W$ is an open globally hyperbolic neighborhood of
$\Sigma$ with $\Sigma$ as a Cauchy hypersurface and $(g,\psi)$ restricts to a
globally hyperbolic development of the data;

**(c)** any two developments as in (a)--(b) of the same data are related near
$\Sigma$ by a data-fixing time-orientation-preserving isometry
([[thm-gr-local-geometric-uniqueness]]).

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$\Sigma\subseteq M$ be a spacelike embedded hypersurface with induced metric
$h$, future unit normal field $n$ and second fundamental form
$K(V,W)=g(\nabla_Vn,W)$ ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]],
[[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]]). Let
$s$ be a smooth function defined near $\Sigma$ with $s=0$ exactly on $\Sigma$
and $ds(n)=1$ (a normal time coordinate), and let $h_0$ be a smooth metric on a
product neighborhood of $\Sigma$ with $h_0|_{\Sigma}=h$ and
$\partial_sh_0=0$. Put $\bar g:=-ds^2+h_0$ as background metric. Define a smooth
metric germ $g_0$ on $\Sigma$ by the initial jet
$$g_{ij}=h_{ij},\qquad g_{00}=-1,\qquad g_{0i}=0,\qquad \partial_sg_{ij}=2K_{ij},\qquad \partial_sg_{0i}=0,\qquad \partial_sg_{00}=-2\operatorname{tr}_hK .$$
Then:

**(a)** $g_0$ is the germ of a smooth Lorentzian metric for which $\Sigma$ is
spacelike with induced metric $h$, future unit normal $n=\partial_s$ and second
fundamental form $K$;

**(b)** the harmonic-gauge vector of $(g_0,\bar g)$ vanishes on $\Sigma$:
$H^a|_\Sigma=0$.

derivations.claim: (Hypotheses.) By [L1] the fluid sector has a first-order quasilinear symmetric hyperbolic reduction with zeroth-order metric coupling; by [L2] its stress tensor is on-shell divergence-free.

(Application.) Applying [L3] to the matter sector described by [L1]--[L2] and to the data $(\Sigma,h,K_2)$ with matter data $(\epsilon_0,n_0)$, whose jet is fixed by [L4], gives the asserted local development, the causal statements and the uniqueness up to a data-fixing isometry.

boundaries.reason: No empty set, empty family or empty index range is formed: the quantified objects (points, fields, mode families, data sets) are nonempty by the hypotheses, and the proofs never split off an empty case.
The value zero is not a distinguished boundary of this claim: no step divides by a quantity that can vanish and no separate zero case is required.
No cardinality-one case is separated: the arguments treat general finite or countable families and the one-element case is included without special treatment.

The hypotheses exclude degenerate configurations: the metric is Lorentzian/nondegenerate, the time matrix or coefficient is positive definite, velocity fields are unit and nonzero where required, and no degenerate limit is claimed.
The assertions are local in open domains around the initial surface or open time intervals, and no endpoint behaviour (completeness, boundary extension or endpoint regularity) is claimed.
No nonconstructive selection from a family is made: the argument uses the objects named in the Given clause and the supplied maps, with at most finite choices.
The item states one-directional implications or constructions, not an equivalence, so no forward direction of an if-and-only-if is asserted.
The item states one-directional implications or constructions, not an equivalence, so no reverse direction of an if-and-only-if is asserted.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, and let $\Sigma\subseteq M$ be a smooth spacelike embedded hypersurface with future unit normal $n$, induced Riemannian metric $h$ and second fundamental form $K(X,Y)=g(\nabla_Xn,Y)$ ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]], [[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]]). Write $D$ for the Levi-Civita connection of $h$, $R^h$ for its curvature operator in the same operator convention as the ambient curvature, and $S_h$ for its scalar curvature. Explicitly distinguish the lowered tensor from the operator pairing by setting
$$\mathcal R^g(A,B,C,D):=g(R^g(C,D)B,A),\qquad \mathcal R^h(A,B,C,D):=h(R^h(C,D)B,A).$$
Thus $\mathcal R^g_{abcd}=R_{abcd}$ in [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]; in particular $g(R^g(X,Y)Z,W)=\mathcal R^g(W,Z,X,Y)$. Let $G$ be the Einstein tensor defined there. At every $p\in\Sigma$ and for all $X,Y,Z,W\in T_p\Sigma$:

**(a) Gauss equation.**
$$\mathcal R^g(X,Y,Z,W)=\mathcal R^h(X,Y,Z,W)+K(X,Z)K(Y,W)-K(X,W)K(Y,Z).$$
Equivalently, in operator order,
$$g(R^g(X,Y)Z,W)=h(R^h(X,Y)Z,W)+K(Y,Z)K(X,W)-K(X,Z)K(Y,W).$$

**(b) Codazzi equation.**
$$g(R^g(X,Y)Z,n)=(D_YK)(X,Z)-(D_XK)(Y,Z).$$

**(c) Normal projections.** Define $(\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)=h^{ij}(D_{e_i}K)(e_j,Y)$, $\tau=\operatorname{tr}_hK=h^{ij}K_{ij}$ and $|K|_h^2=h^{ik}h^{jl}K_{ij}K_{kl}$. Then
$$G(n,n)=\tfrac12(S_h+\tau^2-|K|_h^2),\qquad G(n,Y)=(\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)-D_Y\tau.$$

**(d) Constraint equations.** If the tensor equation $G+\Lambda g=\kappa T$ holds at $p$, for a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor $T$ and real constants $\kappa,\Lambda$, then
$$S_h+\tau^2-|K|_h^2=2\Lambda+2\kappa T(n,n),\qquad (\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)-D_Y\tau=\kappa T(n,Y).$$
With $\rho=T(n,n)$ and $j(Y)=-T(n,Y)$, the second equation is $(\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)-D_Y\tau=-\kappa j(Y)$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]) and let
$U\subseteq M$ be a nonempty open matter domain
([[prop-an-open-subset-of-a-smooth-manifold-has-a-canonical-restricted-smooth-structure]]).

**(a) Data.** A **perfect-fluid model** on $U$ is a triple $(\varepsilon,p,n)$
consisting of two smooth functions $\varepsilon,p:U\to\mathbb R$, the **rest
energy density** and the **pressure**, and a smooth future-directed unit
timelike vector field $n$ on $U$ with $g_p(n_p,n_p)=-1$ and
$g_p(n_p,N_p)<0$ at every $p$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]). No positivity of
$\varepsilon$ or of $p$ is required or implied. A model may carry the
additional data of an **equation of state**: a function
$P:D_P\to\mathbb R$ on a subset $D_P\subseteq\mathbb R$ with
$\varepsilon(U)\subseteq D_P$, together with the relation $p=P(\varepsilon)$;
the relation is a further assumption and is not part of the basic triple.

**(b) Stress-energy tensor and derived fields.** The model's
**stress-energy tensor** is

$$T^{ab}:=(\varepsilon+p)n^an^b+p\,g^{ab},$$

a smooth symmetric contravariant $2$-tensor field ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]],
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]). The **comoving
derivative**, **expansion** and **acceleration** of $n$ are

$$D f:=n^a\partial_af\quad(f\in C^\infty(U)),\qquad \vartheta:=\nabla_an^a,\qquad a^b:=n^a\nabla_an^b ,$$

and the **rest-space projection** is the smooth tensor field

$$h^{ab}:=g^{ab}+n^an^b .$$

The physical reading of $\varepsilon$ and $p$ as a rest-frame energy density
and pressure, and their units, are fixed by the framework's matter postulate,
not by this definition.

**(c) Fluid equations.** The **perfect-fluid equations** on $U$ are

$$D\varepsilon+(\varepsilon+p)\vartheta=0,\qquad (\varepsilon+p)a^b+h^{ba}\partial_ap=0 .$$

That the stress-energy tensor is divergence-free if and only if these two
equations hold is proved in
[[prop-gr-dust-and-perfect-fluid-conservation-equations]]; the definition
asserts neither divergence-freedom nor the equations.
